chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who embraced Islam during
the middle of the month of Ramadan, what is upon him regarding his fasting? He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him except for what he embraced Islam in.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for someone who converts to Islam in the middle of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a new convert is exempt from making up the days of Ramadan they missed prior to their conversion, as the obligation of fasting begins from the moment of embracing Islam. This ruling highlights the principle that religious duties are incumbent only upon those who have reached the threshold of accountability (mukallaf) and are aware of the command, reflecting the Shia juristic view that prior ignorance or non-membership exempts one from retrospective obligations. The hadith underscores the mercy and practicality in Islamic law, ensuring that new Muslims are not burdened with compensating for periods when they were not yet subject to the Sharia's specific mandates.
